title: EHR Read-Only Access — Interface Engine Still Stuck

fields.to: Director of IT, Chief Nursing Officer, Administrator on Call
fields.subject: FW: EHR Read-Only Access — Interface Engine Still Stuck
fields.note:
The C-212 core is now carrying the clinical VLANs. The LIS came back at 18:20, but ORRMC-INT01 is still stuck in a restart loop. Results are flowing from lab to EHR but not back. The EHR is accessible read-only on 60 workstations across the campus. I’ve confirmed with Clinical Engineering that the device network (10.40.x.x) is stable and pumps and monitors are operating normally.

If we allow clinical units to begin charting in the EHR now, we risk a split record: 4–5 hours of paper documentation will need to be re-keyed into the EHR later, and the record will be fragmented across systems. The EHR may drop again if the interface engine fails.

Recommendation: keep paper as the active record for orders and medications. Use the EHR only to read lab results, imaging reports, and medication histories. I’ll send a broadcast to all units to clarify what the screens will and will not show.
fields.signature:
Raymond Okafor
Director of IT
Ottawa River Regional Medical Center

original.subject: Interface Engine ORRMC-INT01 stuck in restart loop
original.body:
ORRMC-INT01 is not completing startup. The interface engine is still in a restart loop after 30 minutes. The other engine, ORRMC-INT02, is in standby and not active. The lab system (ORRMC-LIS01) is back online and sending results to the EHR, but the EHR cannot send orders or patient data back to the lab.

We have not yet disabled the engine. No restarts have been attempted on ORRMC-INT01.

Status: Interface engine operational status = 'Failed to Start'

We are awaiting direction from the IT leadership.

instructorNote: This inject triggers the AOC to confirm the decision to use EHR only for read access. The CNO must verify that paper procedures are still in force for orders and medications, and the DIT must clarify the EHR's read-only status to all units. Watch for confusion over what the EHR can and cannot do.
